title: Tenant fencing and trace hook expansion for VPC/on-prem observability
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Extend tracing hooks and ingest pipeline transforms for VPC/on-prem collectors to provide strong tenant fencing, burst isolation, and tenant-level observability. This ticket covers SDK trace-hook extensions, signed telemetry envelopes for on-prem collectors, adaptive per-tenant buffering, and new latency/error dashboards that make tenant-level degradation visible without compromising cross-tenant isolation.
acceptance_criteria: Trace SDK includes tenant-scoped hook that injects a strong tenant_id header and signed envelope metadata for on-prem collectors
Collector pipeline enforces per-tenant buffer caps and a soft-fence mode that can early-drop noisy tenants with configurable thresholds
Pipeline transform removes PII fields from logs and spans for private deployments (configurable allowlist) and logs transformation actions to an audit stream
New Grafana dashboards: per-tenant ingest latency, per-tenant dropped-span rate, queue depth heatmap, and cross-tenant SLA dashboard are deployed to staging and accessible to SRE
End-to-end test: simulated burst from one tenant does not increase P99 latency for other tenants above SLO in a 3-node on-prem collector cluster
Rollout plan executed as canary to 5% of Dedicated customers then ramp with automatic rollback on high dropped-span rates
decision_log: Chose signed telemetry envelopes (HMAC + key rotation) over full KMS-wrapped signatures for initial rollout to reduce latency and avoid HSM dependencies
Implemented soft-fence mode (early drop with telemetry and alerting) instead of immediate hard-quarantine to reduce false positives during noisy workload spikes
Will use per-tenant token buckets combined with queue-based admission to give burst allowance but enforce steady-state fairness
Dashboarding will be metric-first (Prometheus/Grafana) with a telemetry-derived incident runbook link rather than adding heavy trace queries to the initial view

2026-02-27 - Priya Rao (SRE): Load test scenario v1: a single tenant bursted 10x baseline for 15 minutes. Observed queue build up but no cross-tenant latency increase in single-zone sim. Will run multi-zone test next.
2026-03-03 - Security review: require explicit allowlist config for PII fields and audit stream of removals. Also requested threat model doc. Added to links.
2026-03-08 - Design feedback (Marco): Dashboard should include a tenant-health score and a link to quota and billing page for faster remediation by support.
2026-03-10 - Liam Chen: Merged pipeline transform PR to staging, starting canary rollout to two on-prem clusters for partners. Monitoring alerts configured for dropped-span rate > 0.5% sustained 5m.
engineering_notes: Collector change: add tenant-bounded queue per tenant sharded by tenant hash to avoid head-of-line blocking
SDK change: add beforeSendTrace(hooks) that returns envelope metadata; default implementation attaches tenant_id, sampling_status, and envelope_signature
Backpressure strategy: circuit-breaker per tenant that toggles soft-fence when queue depth > 80% for >30s
Observability: emit metrics tenant.ingest.latency_seconds{quantile}, tenant.ingest.dropped_spans_total, tenant.queue.depth, tenant.envelope.signature_errors_total
Testing: deterministic replay harness to emulate bursts and validate that other tenants maintain P99 latency within SLO
Ops: Runbook stub added to confluence with steps to identify noisy tenant, escalate, throttle, and communicate to customer
